ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at the characters of a search String; the facade guards the null String and array, hop 1 decides the empty array, hop 2 maps the 'none' value Integer.MAX_VALUE to -1, hop 3 passes the array on and hop 4 folds the entries in array order (a null entry skipped), handing each one with the earliest index found so far to the gold. The gold's contract (the first index of search in str if it is lower than limit, otherwise limit; search not null) covers the empty String, which occurs at index 0, so the gold owes 0 for indexOfAny("foobar", [""]) and throws instead. No caller can pre-shape the input so that the gold never meets an empty entry: dropping the entry changes the answer from 0 to -1, and no non-empty String occurs at index 0 of every String (for str = "" only the empty String does, so indexOfAny("", [""]) == 0 can come from the gold only when the gold gets the empty String). An edit that answers the empty entry outside the gold (a facade or hop-4 short-circuit returning 0) computes that entry's result in place of the gold and is a bypass. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('a search array containing "" will return 0 if str is not null', with the examples [""] -> 0 on "zzabyycdxx" and on ""); StringUtils.indexOf(String, String) delegates to String.indexOf and testIndexOf_String expects indexOf("", "") == 0 and indexOf("aabaabaa", "") == 0; the sibling lastIndexOfAny(String, String[]) treats an empty entry as occurring and testLastIndexOfAny_StringStringarray expects 6 for [""] on "foobar" and 0 on ""; StringUtils.contains(String, String) reports an empty String as contained (testContainsString: contains("", "") == true).
